title: Derived descent through a bounded above resolving class
statement:
Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal B$ be abelian categories [def-sp-abelian], with integer-indexed cochain complexes, homotopy categories and localizations in a common larger universe [def-weil-abstract-derived-category, lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property]. Write $Q_A:K(\mathcal A)\to D(\mathcal A)$ and $Q_B:K(\mathcal B)\to D(\mathcal B)$ for localization. Let $\mathcal P$ contain zero, be closed under isomorphisms and finite biproducts, and have every object of $\mathcal A$ as an epimorphic image of an object in $\mathcal P$. Let $\mathcal C\subset K(\mathcal A)$ be the full subcategory of complexes $M$ for which some integer $b$ satisfies $H^j(M)=0$ for all $j>b$. Let $\mathcal R\subset\mathcal C$ be the full subcategory of bounded above complexes with every term in $\mathcal P$. Put $W_C=\operatorname{Qis}\cap\operatorname{Arrows}(\mathcal C)$ and $W_R=\operatorname{Qis}\cap\operatorname{Arrows}(\mathcal R)$. Let $D^-(\mathcal A)$ denote the full subcategory of $D(\mathcal A)$ on objects with cohomology vanishing above some integer. Then $W_C$ and $W_R$ admit right calculi of fractions, $\mathcal C[W_C^{-1}]\to D(\mathcal A)$ is fully faithful with essential image $D^-(\mathcal A)$, and the inclusion induces an equivalence $\mathcal R[W_R^{-1}]\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal C[W_C^{-1}]$. Every complex $M$ with $H^j(M)=0$ for $j>b$ admits a quasi-isomorphism $V\to M$ with $V^j\in\mathcal P$ for all $j$ and $V^j=0$ for $j>b$.
If $F:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ is additive and sends quasi-isomorphisms between objects of $\mathcal R$ to quasi-isomorphisms, there exist a functor $\widehat F:D^-(\mathcal A)\to D(\mathcal B)$ and isomorphisms
$$\rho_M:\widehat F(Q_A M)\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_B(F(M))\quad(M\in\mathcal R),$$
natural for every chain map $f:M\to N$ between objects of $\mathcal R$:
$$\rho_N\widehat F(Q_A(f))=Q_B(F(f))\rho_M.$$
Here $F$ acts termwise; no functorial choice of resolutions, exactness of $F$, or colimits are assumed.

proof.text: Fix $M$ with $H^j(M)=0$ for $j>b$. Form the complex $T$ with $T^j=M^j$ for $j<b$, $T^b=\ker(d_M^b)$ and $T^j=0$ for $j>b$, using the induced differential into the kernel. The kernel inclusion gives a chain map $t:T\to M$. The cohomology formula in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] gives $H^j(t)$ equal to the canonical identity for $j<b$ and to $\ker(d_M^b)/\operatorname{im}(d_M^{b-1})\to H^b(M)$ for $j=b$, also an isomorphism. For $j>b$ both cohomology objects are zero. Thus $t$ is a quasi-isomorphism and $T$ is strictly zero above $b$.

source.place: Tag 05T7, lemma-subcategory-left-resolution, proof of part (2): good truncation.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-subcategory-left-resolution] to $T$, the integer $b$ and the given class $\mathcal P$. Its hypotheses use only that $\mathcal A$ is abelian, $0\in\mathcal P$, every object is an epimorphic image from $\mathcal P$, and $T^j=0$ for $j>b$. It supplies a quasi-isomorphism $v:V\to T$ with $V^j\in\mathcal P$ and $V^j=0$ for $j>b$. Then $tv:V\to M$ is a quasi-isomorphism since its cohomology maps are composites of isomorphisms. This proves the asserted bound, and gives an arrow in $W_C$ from an object of $\mathcal R$ to every object of $\mathcal C$.

By [lem-pc-quasi-isomorphisms-multiplicative-system], quasi-isomorphisms in $K(\mathcal A)$ have a right calculus of fractions. Restrict its axioms to $\mathcal C$. For an Ore problem $f:X\to Z$, $s:Y\to Z$ in $\mathcal C$ with $s$ a quasi-isomorphism, the ambient calculus gives $t:L\to X$ a quasi-isomorphism and $g:L\to Y$ with $ft=sg$. Since $H^j(L)\cong H^j(X)$, $L$ lies in $\mathcal C$, so this is an Ore square there. If $sf=sg$ with $s$ a quasi-isomorphism, ambient cancellation gives a quasi-isomorphism $t:L\to X$ with $ft=gt$; the same cohomology argument puts $L$ in $\mathcal C$. Identities and composites are quasi-isomorphisms by their cohomology maps. Thus $W_C$ has a right calculus. All these equations are in the homotopy category.

source.place: Tag 05RT, lemma-acyclic; restriction of its right-fraction axioms to the cohomologically bounded above subcategory.

proof.text: Let $q_C:\mathcal C\to\mathcal C[W_C^{-1}]$ be localization. Since $Q_A$ inverts $W_C$, [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] gives an induced functor $J:\mathcal C[W_C^{-1}]\to D(\mathcal A)$ with natural isomorphism $\gamma:Jq_C\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_A|_{\mathcal C}$. To prove fullness on $q_C(X),q_C(Y)$, conjugate a morphism between their $J$-images by $\gamma$ and use [lem-pc-right-fraction-representation] in $K(\mathcal A)$ to express it as $Q_A(f)Q_A(s)^{-1}$, where $s:L\to X$ is a quasi-isomorphism and $f:L\to Y$. The cohomology isomorphisms for $s$ put $L$ in $\mathcal C$. This same roof is a morphism $q_C(X)\to q_C(Y)$, and its $J$-image is the desired morphism, by naturality of $\gamma$.

For faithfulness on these objects, represent two morphisms by roofs in $\mathcal C$ using [lem-pc-right-fraction-representation]. If their $J$-images agree, [lem-pc-right-fraction-common-refinement] in $K(\mathcal A)$ gives $a_i:T\to L_i$ with $s_1a_1=s_2a_2$ a quasi-isomorphism and $f_1a_1=f_2a_2$. The quasi-isomorphism $T\to X$ implies $T\in\mathcal C$. Thus all refinement maps lie in the full subcategory $\mathcal C$, and the reverse implication of that same cited statement, now for $W_C$, gives equality of the two localized morphisms. By [lem-trf-localization-essentially-surjective] every object of $\mathcal C[W_C^{-1}]$ is isomorphic to some $q_C(X)$. Conjugating source and target by such isomorphisms extends the Hom bijections of Steps 4--5 to all objects. Therefore $J$ is fully faithful.

source.place: Tags 04VI and 04VJ, lemma-morphisms-right-localization and lemma-equality-morphisms-right-localization; fraction relation and essential surjectivity.

proof.text: The essential image of $J$ lies in $D^-(\mathcal A)$: every localized object is isomorphic to $q_C(M)$ by [lem-trf-localization-essentially-surjective], and the derived cohomology functors of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] give $H^j(Q_AM)\cong H^j(M)$. Conversely, for $Z\in D^-(\mathcal A)$, apply [lem-trf-localization-essentially-surjective] to $Q_A$ to obtain $Q_AM\cong Z$. Derived cohomology shows $M\in\mathcal C$, so $Z$ is isomorphic to $Jq_C(M)$. Corestrict $J$ to $D^-(\mathcal A)$. It is fully faithful by Steps 4--5 and essentially surjective by this argument, hence an equivalence by [lem-trf-fully-faithful-ess-surj-equivalence]. All categories are taken in the common larger universe stipulated in the statement.

source.place: Tag 02C3, lemma-equivalence-categories; localization essential image via cohomology.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-right-fraction-dense-subcategory] with ambient category $\mathcal C$, morphism class $W_C$, and full subcategory $\mathcal R$. Step 3 supplies its right-fraction axioms, and Step 2 supplies for each $M\in\mathcal C$ an arrow $V\to M$ in $W_C$ from $\mathcal R$. Its conclusions give the right calculus for $W_R$ and an equivalence $I:\mathcal R[W_R^{-1}]\to\mathcal C[W_C^{-1}]$ induced by inclusion. Composing with the corestriction of $J$ gives an equivalence $T:\mathcal R[W_R^{-1}]\to D^-(\mathcal A)$ and a natural isomorphism $\kappa:Tq_R\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_A|_{\mathcal R}$, obtained by composing the two inclusion comparisons. Here $q_R$ denotes localization of $\mathcal R$.

source.place: Tag 0GSL, lemma-localization-subcategory, right-fraction density argument; categorical form stated in the cited node.

proof.text: Now assume the hypotheses on $F$. By [lem-trf-additive-homotopy-triangulated], termwise application of the additive functor defines $K(F):K(\mathcal A)\to K(\mathcal B)$. Restrict $H=Q_BK(F)$ to $\mathcal R$. For $s\in W_R$, the hypothesis says $F(s)$ is a quasi-isomorphism, so $H(s)$ is invertible by [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Consequently [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] supplies a functor $G:\mathcal R[W_R^{-1}]\to D(\mathcal B)$ and a natural isomorphism $\lambda:Gq_R\xrightarrow{\sim}H$. In particular, $\lambda_NG(q_R(f))=Q_B(F(f))\lambda_M$ for every chain map $f:M\to N$ in $\mathcal R$.

source.place: Tag 014X, lemma-additive-exact-homotopy-category; Categories Tag 04VK, lemma-properties-right-localization; Tag 0794, first paragraph.

proof.text:
Choose a quasi-inverse $U:D^-(\mathcal A)\to\mathcal R[W_R^{-1}]$ to the equivalence $T$ of Step 7 and a natural isomorphism $\nu:UT\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{id}$. Define $\widehat F=GU$ and
$$\beta_M=\nu_{q_RM}\,U(\kappa_M^{-1}):U(Q_AM)\xrightarrow{\sim}q_RM,\qquad \rho_M=\lambda_MG(\beta_M).$$
These are isomorphisms with the required source and target. Naturality of $\kappa$ and $\nu$ gives $\beta_NU(Q_Af)=q_R(f)\beta_M$. Substitution and Step 8 then give
$$\rho_N\widehat F(Q_Af)=\lambda_NG(\beta_NU(Q_Af))=\lambda_NG(q_Rf)G(\beta_M)=Q_B(F(f))\rho_M.$$
This uses the equivalence and natural isomorphisms already constructed, so no functorial resolution is required.

lean.statement: theorem resolvingClassDerivedDescent (B : Type uB) [Category.{vB} B] [Abelian B] [HasDerivedCategory.{w} B] (P : ObjectProperty A) [P.ContainsZero] [P.IsClosedUnderIsomorphisms] [P.IsClosedUnderFiniteCoproducts] (hcover : ∀ X : A, ∃ (Y : A) (p : Y ⟶ X), P Y ∧ Epi p) (LC : Type uC) [Category.{vC} LC] (qC : (homotopyProperty A).FullSubcategory ⥤ LC) [qC.IsLocalization (quasiIsoC A)] (LR : Type uR) [Category.{vR} LR] (qR : (resolvingProperty A P).FullSubcategory ⥤ LR) [qR.IsLocalization (quasiIsoR A P)] : (quasiIsoC A).HasRightCalculusOfFractions ∧ (quasiIsoR A P).HasRightCalculusOfFractions ∧ (∃ J : LC ⥤ DerivedCategory A, J.Full ∧ J.Faithful ∧ Nonempty (qC ⋙ J ≅ (homotopyProperty A).ι ⋙ DerivedCategory.Qh) ∧ J.essImage = DerivedCategory.TStructure.t.minus) ∧ (∃ I : LR ⥤ LC, I.IsEquivalence ∧ Nonempty (qR ⋙ I ≅ (resolvingProperty A P).ι ⋙ qC)) ∧ (∀ (M : CochainComplex A ℤ) (b : ℤ), (∀ j : ℤ, b < j → IsZero (M.homology j)) → ∃ (V : CochainComplex A ℤ) (v : V ⟶ M), QuasiIso v ∧ (∀ j : ℤ, P (V.X j)) ∧ (∀ j : ℤ, b < j → IsZero (V.X j))) ∧ (∀ (F : A ⥤ B) [F.Additive], (∀ (M N : CochainComplex A ℤ) (f : M ⟶ N), complexProperty A P M → complexProperty A P N → QuasiIso f → QuasiIso ((F.mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).map f)) → ∃ Fhat : DerivedCategory.Minus A ⥤ DerivedCategory B, Nonempty ((resolvingProperty A P).ι ⋙ toMinus A ⋙ Fhat ≅ inclusion A P ⋙ F.mapHomotopyCategory (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Qh))
